All Native Group, a division of Ho Chunk Incorporated, is seeking a Junior Data Scientist to support a Federal Agency enterprise data management and analytics program. This role supports the Analytic team in developing machine learning models, preparing and analyzing data, and applying natural language processing to unstructured datasets. It is an excellent opportunity for an emerging data scientist to grow within a high-impact federal mission environment. This position supports an active federal contract. Any offer of employment is contingent upon Government approval of the candidate and successful completion of the DEA security clearance process.

Essential Functions

• Support the development, training, and evaluation of machine learning and AI models under the direction of the Analytic Lead and senior data scientists.

• Apply NLP techniques to extract and enrich unstructured data.

• Assist in expanding entity extraction by preparing data, testing models, and documenting results.

• Cleanse and prepare structured and unstructured data for model development.

• Build data visualizations that communicate findings to technical and non-technical audiences.

• Participate in Agile ceremonies, including stand-ups, sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives.

Competencies

• 2+ years of experience with an analytical or statistical language such as Python, R, or SQL.

• Exposure to machine learning concepts, including model training and evaluation.

• Experience working with structured and unstructured data.

• Familiarity with data visualization tools.

• Ability to work collaboratively in an Agile development environment.

Work is conducted at the DEA facilities in Arlington, VA and Merrifield, VA. This is a full-time position with flexible hours based on mission requirements.

What are Trust Fund Positions?

Trust Fund positions are unique to the Smithsonian. They are paid for from a variety of sources, including the Smithsonian endowment, revenue from our business activities, donations, grants and contracts. Trust employees are not part of the civil service, nor does trust fund employment lead to Federal status. The salary ranges for trust positions are generally the same as for federal positions and in many cases trust and federal employees work side by side. Trust employees have their own benefit program, which may include Health, Dental & Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Transit/Commuter Benefits, Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, Annual and Sick Leave, Family Friendly Leave, 403b Retirement Plan, Discounts for Smithsonian Memberships, Museum Stores and Restaurants, Credit Union, Smithsonian Early Enrichment Center (Child Care), Flexible Spending Account (Health & Dependent Care).
Conditions of Employment

• Pass Pre-employment Background Check and Subsequent Background Investigation for position designated.

• Complete a Probationary Period.

• Maintain a Bank Account for Direct Deposit/Electronic Transfer.

• The position is open to all candidates eligible to work in the United States. Proof of eligibility to work in U.S. is not required to apply.

• Applicants must meet all qualification and eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement.

OVERVIEW
This position is located in Washington, DC, within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO), Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI), under the Office of the Under Secretary for Science and Research at the Smithsonian Institution (SI).

STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests.

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Data Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)

• Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.

• Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.

• Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.

• Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.

• Processes, validates, organizes, and manages tree inventory, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS), and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data for scientific analysis and long-term storage.

• Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.

• Develops and maintains data-management solutions and informatics workflows for data acquisition, formatting, validation, processing, analysis, use, and storage.

• Implements established data standards and contributes to the development and modification of data structures and architectures appropriate to assigned projects.

• Writes, tests, documents, troubleshoots, and maintains computer code used in data-processing and analytical workflows.

• Uses programming languages and tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, GIS applications, and related scientific and data-management software.

• Identifies data-quality problems, inconsistencies, missing values, formatting issues, and other anomalies and determines appropriate methods for correcting or documenting them.

• Works with researchers and other technical personnel to ensure that processed data and analyticalproducts meet established scientific and program requirements.

Requirements Gathering and Technical Support (25%)

• Works closely with researchers and program personnel to identify data-processing, analytical, software, and data-management requirements for assigned scientific projects.

• Conducts technical analyses of available methods and alternatives and recommends appropriate software tools, workflows, calculations, and analytical approaches.

• Assists researchers in translating scientific requirements into practical data-processing and

• computational solutions.

• Evaluates existing workflows and recommends modifications when established approaches do not fully address the characteristics of the data or requirements of an assigned project.

• Coordinates with site representatives concerning timelines and technical requirements for acquisition and submission of plot inventory, TLS, ALS, GNSS, and related scientific data.

• Reviews submitted data to determine whether established ForestGEO and GEO-TREES formatting, documentation, and data-quality requirements have been met.

• Works with site personnel to resolve routine and moderately complex data-submission and data-quality problems.

• Coordinates with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) and other appropriate technical staff to ensure assigned development activities follow applicable systems-development, documentation, version-control, security, and software-development practices.

• Prepares technical documentation describing data-processing workflows, code, data structures, analytical procedures, and related methods.

• Assists in testing new or modified software tools, workflows, and procedures prior to implementation.

Training and Collaboration (25%)

• Develops and provides formal and informal training to researchers, site personnel, and program partners concerning ForestGEO and GEO-TREES data systems, data-management procedures, formatting requirements, data-processing workflows, and related tools.

• Serves as a technical point of contact for tree-inventory teams and other users at assigned ForestGEO and GEO-TREES sites.

• Provides advice, training, troubleshooting assistance, and technical support concerning data collection, formatting, cleaning, validation, processing, documentation, and submission.

• Explains data standards, analytical procedures, software requirements, and data-management practices to researchers and partners with varying levels of technical expertise.

• Collaborates with scientists, data managers, programmers, and other personnel to identify and resolve data-management and processing problems.

• Participates in meetings, working groups, and collaborative activities involving ForestGEO, GEO-TREES, Smithsonian staff, and domestic and international research partners.

• Shares information concerning lessons learned, recurring data problems, workflow improvements, and effective data-management practices with program staff and partners.

Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
Education and Experience:

• Professional knowledge of and skill in applying a wide range of data-science principles, concepts, methods, and practices sufficient to perform difficult data-management, processing, computational, and analytical assignments involving ecological and forestry data.

• Knowledge of data acquisition, data cleaning, validation, transformation, integration, storage, analysis, visualization, documentation, and reproducible computational workflows.

• Knowledge of computational and data-management methods is required to develop, modify, implement, and maintain processing pipelines for tree inventory, GNSS, ALS, TLS, spatial, and related scientific datasets.

• Knowledge of programming concepts and skill in applying programming languages and analytical tools such as R, Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, and related software to manipulate, process, analyze, and manage scientific data.

• Knowledge of algorithm development, software testing, version control, debugging, documentation, deployment, and maintenance practices is required to support scientific applications and data-processing workflows.

• Knowledge of spatial-data concepts, common spatial-data formats, and GIS software is required to process and evaluate geospatial information associated with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES projects.

• Knowledge of the scientific concepts associated with ecology, tropical biology, forestry, or related environmental sciences sufficient to understand data characteristics, research requirements, analytical objectives, and the relationships among data variables.

• Knowledge to select and modify appropriate data-processing and analytical methods; identify and resolve data-quality problems; evaluate alternative computational approaches; interpret results; develop recommendations; and prepare technical documentation and analytical products.

• Skill adapting or modifying established data-science techniques and procedures to address differences in data structure, quality, collection methods, analytical requirements, or site-specific circumstances.

OUR COMPANY

Iron EagleX (IEX), a wholly owned subsidiary of General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT), delivers agile IT and Intelligence solutions. Combining small-team flexibility with global scale, IEX leverages emerging technologies to provide innovative, user-focused solutions that empower organizations and end users to operate smarter, faster, and more securely in dynamic environments.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Iron EagleX is seeking a Senior Principal Data Scientist to join our dynamic team in Crystal City, VA. This role creates and delivers innovative analytic solutions as a member of a fast-paced, multidisciplinary team. You will work directly with large, complex, and disparate datasets to develop practical analytic methods, identify meaningful patterns and relationships, and translate technical findings into capabilities and insights that support critical customer requirements.

MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT

As a Senior Principal Data Scientist, you will quickly turn large and complex datasets into clear, actionable insights for critical customer requirements. You will work closely with analysts, software developers, and other technical specialists to solve difficult data problems, develop new analytic approaches, and transition successful methods from exploratory analysis into repeatable and operational capabilities.

JOB DUTIES (INCLUDE BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO)

• Implement structured, repeatable data analysis across large, disparate datasets to surface patterns, trends, anomalies, relationships, and other signals in support of mission and analytic needs.

• Explore and characterize unfamiliar datasets, including assessing data quality, completeness, distributions, relationships, and limitations to determine appropriate analytic approaches and identify potentially useful signals.

• Develop, maintain, and improve analytic tooling such as queries, scripts, notebooks, lightweight services, and reusable code components to automate recurring workflows and enable rapid analysis.

• Develop and evaluate applied statistical, machine learning, and algorithmic approaches for problems such as classification, clustering, anomaly detection, similarity analysis, prioritization, entity resolution, relationship discovery, and predictive analysis.

• Establish appropriate validation methods, benchmarks, scoring approaches, thresholds, and measures of confidence to evaluate analytic performance and clearly communicate the strengths and limitations of analytic results.

• Build and enhance interactive analytic dashboards and lightweight GUIs, such as Streamlit applications, that support data exploration, linkage review, analyst workflows, model or algorithm evaluation, and generation of structured outputs.

• Create analyst-ready products, including tables, visualizations, summaries, briefings, and structured exports, that translate technical findings into clear, decision-oriented insights.

• Work with analysts, engineers, and technical staff to convert ad hoc analyses and successful prototypes into reusable pipelines, standardized methodologies, documented workflows, and maintainable analytic capabilities.

• Support the integration, testing, and refinement of analytic methods in operational environments, ensuring outputs are reproducible, explainable, and usable by both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Document analytic assumptions, methodologies, data transformations, validation approaches, and known limitations to promote reproducibility, peer review, and continued improvement of analytic capabilities.

REQUIRED SKILLS:

• Strong Python skills for building practical analytic solutions, including data processing, automation, exploratory analysis, visualization, algorithm development, and reproducible scripts or notebooks using libraries such as pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, or similar tools.

• Strong SQL and hands-on experience working directly with large datasets in modern data platforms such as Trino, PostgreSQL, Hive, OpenSearch, or Elasticsearch; experience working with distributed query or large-scale data environments is strongly preferred.

• Experience applying statistical, machine learning, or algorithmic techniques to real-world datasets, with the ability to select appropriate approaches based on the characteristics of the data and the operational problem rather than relying solely on predefined models or techniques.

• Experience designing and implementing repeatable analytic workflows, including source triage, exploratory data analysis, data profiling, quality checks, transformation logic, feature development, validation, documentation, and reusable code patterns.

• Practical experience developing analytic methods for entity resolution, relationship discovery, graph and relational analysis, including implementation of scoring, thresholds, validation checks, and measures of analytic confidence.

• Experience evaluating analytic methods using appropriate metrics, baselines, test datasets, sensitivity analysis, or other validation approaches and identifying sources of error, uncertainty, or degraded performance.

• Experience integrating structured, semi-structured, and text-based data, including extracting key fields and signals, normalizing data across sources, resolving inconsistencies, and combining schemas to support downstream analysis and tooling.

• Ability to independently investigate complex or poorly defined analytic problems, rapidly become familiar with unfamiliar datasets, formulate testable approaches, and iteratively refine solutions based on results and stakeholder feedback.

• Ability to translate technical analysis into usable outputs for analysts and decisionmakers, including clear visualizations, concise analytic narratives, dashboards, structured deliverables, and explanations of analytic confidence and limitations.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams that include analysts, data scientists, data engineers, software engineers, and mission stakeholders.

DESIRED SKILLS

• Experience with applied machine learning techniques such as classification, clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection, ranking, similarity analysis, natural language processing, or time-series analysis.

• Experience working with graph-based data and analytics, including knowledge graphs, network analysis, graph databases, or techniques for identifying relationships and communities across interconnected data.

• Experience working with geospatial, temporal, or other specialized data types and incorporating spatial or time-dependent relationships into analytic workflows.

• Familiarity with modern AI and large language model capabilities, including using LLMs for information extraction, classification, summarization, entity identification, or other components of broader data science and analytic workflows.

• Experience developing or integrating APIs and lightweight Python services, such as FastAPI, to expose analytic methods or data science capabilities to downstream applications and users.

• Familiarity with deploying applications and analytic capabilities in Dockerized environments and utilizing CI/CD pipelines to support repeatable, secure, and maintainable software delivery.

• Familiarity with Git best practices, including branching strategies, pull requests, code reviews, merge conflict resolution, and maintaining clean, well-documented repositories.

• Experience integrating React-based frontends with RESTful APIs and Python-based backend services.

• Familiarity with large-scale data processing technologies such as Apache Iceberg, Spark, object storage platforms, or similar modern data architectures.

• Experience working in multidisciplinary environments where data science capabilities must be transitioned from exploratory research or prototyping into reliable, maintainable operational tools.

Team Description
The Beyond AML Modeling & Innovations (BAMI) team within the Enterprise Risk Organization leverages AI to modernize and transform how we assess risk. We are a small but mighty team of data scientists and business analysts who partner closely with stakeholders to design and deploy innovative solutions. In this role, you will have the opportunity to drive a variety of 0-to-1 projects, utilizing traditional machine learning, natural language processing, graph-based modeling, and Generative AI and more to solve novel, complex challenges. Senior Data Scientist, ML- Fraud Detection & Effectiveness

The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Senior Machine Learning Data Scientist to build fraud and abuse detection models and measure how effectively they work. This role combines hands-on modeling with deep experimentation, evaluation, and analytics to improve detection and quantify business impact.

You will work across the fraud lifecycle - from modeling and ground-truth definition to performance measurement, monitoring, and executive-ready insights!
What you'll Do
• Build and tune ML models for fraud and abuse detection using statistical and classical ML techniques.
• Develop robust evaluation frameworks, datasets, and metrics to measure model and mitigation effectiveness.
• Analyze false positives/negatives, model drift, and emerging fraud patterns to continuously improve detection.
• Define ground truth, labeling approaches, and fraud taxonomies that support reliable model development and evaluation.
• Design experiments and evaluate tradeoffs across precision, recall, customer impact, and fraud loss.
• Build dashboards and metrics that translate detection performance into measurable business impact.
• Pressure-test models and data for leakage, bias, data-quality issues, and other sources of misleading results.
• Partner across engineering, product, policy, and risk teams to turn insights into detection improvements and business decisions.
What you'll need to succeed
• 8+ years in applied Data Science / ML, with experience building and evaluating production ML models.
• Strong foundation in statistical and classical ML, experimentation, model evaluation, and performance measurement.
• Strong hands-on Python and SQL skills working with large, complex datasets.
• Experience with model monitoring, drift, false-positive/false-negative analysis, and imperfect or delayed labels.
• Strong data visualization and storytelling skills - able to translate complex analysis into clear insights and recommendations.
• Strong analytical judgment, ownership, and ability to operate independently through ambiguity.
• Bachelor's or equivalent experience in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related field; advanced degree a plus.
Preferred Attributes
• Experience in fraud, abuse, risk, identity, trust & safety, or other adversarial domains.
• Experience with anomaly detection, clustering, behavioral modeling, or prevalence estimation.
• Experience with labeling frameworks, weak supervision, active learning, or human-review systems.
